message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to very different lineages—Felidae in the order **Carnivora** and Equidae in the order **Perissodactyla**.  
Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the ancestor of the clade that contains both of those orders, i.e. the ancestor of the larger clade that gives rise to all placental mammals (Eutheria). In other words, the last common ancestor of a lion and a zebra was a small, probably insect‑eating mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago, before the split between the lineages that led to modern carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates.
